answer: Give each applicant one jade astrolabe calibrated to one harbor's tide table. Each voyage leg starts only after the holder files a sextant reading whose delta in tide height matches the measured value, so legs run in order and one astrolabe serves no second holder. A copied reading fails: each harbor's tide curve is distinct and shifts daily, so a replay never matches a fresh measurement. Fitting one astrolabe costs $480 plus 24 charting hours; 5,000 identities would need 5,000 astrolabes, $2,400,000 and 120,000 hours, because no workshop calibrates a second stone to the same tide curve.
